author: Claude
headline: All eyes on Anthropic's Nasdaq debut. Walmart raises its outlook
summary: Ahead of the US open, Anthropic is set to start trading on Nasdaq in what is expected to be the largest IPO on record, and chip stocks are being lifted by the excitement. Walmart raised its outlook despite soaring fuel costs, although early reports show its shares slipping after the results. Nerves have eased a little, with the VIX fear gauge down 9% to 22.4. In London the FTSE 100 is down 0.4%: consumer names like Unilever, Reckitt and JD Sports fell while miners bounced back. The backdrop is still Cautious, so the picks favour steady companies.
points: SSE, the UK wind-power and electricity network company, joins the picks. Legal & General drops out after RBC cut its forecasts for L&G's pension deals.
London consumer stocks fell: JD Sports 3.9%, Reckitt 2.8% and Unilever 2.7%. Miners bounced, with Anglo American up 2.9%.
Gold is having a bad year and slipped another 0.6%, while oil edged up 0.6%.
Fed officials have signalled more rate rises, which keeps pressure on expensive growth stocks even as AI excitement returns.
Bitcoin is up 1.1% at about $63,700, but Bitcoin funds are seeing money flow out and every major cryptocurrency is still in a downtrend.
